item.title: A billion seconds is 31 years. AI skeptics are making the same mistake.
item.description: AI success on open-ended problems jumped from 25% to 76% in eight months. That’s the headline number in Anthropic’s recent post. The one I keep coming back to is two paragraphs further down. The time it takes for task length to double has itself dropped, from seven months to four. The curve’s going up, and it’s steepening as it goes.1

item.title: Grand Theory of AI Skepticism (In UX Research)
item.description:
Most cynicism about AI in UX research is two years stale.

I spend a lot of time on r/UXResearch and on calls with researchers using Great Question. The same misperceptions come up in both. Confidently, often in upvoted comments, often in the same breath as “I haven’t actually tried it lately.”

item.title: You Have to Touch AI Psychosis
item.description:
Still from The Shining (1980), dir. Stanley Kubrick.

Andrej Karpathy hasn’t handwritten a line of code since December. His ratio of typed-to-delegated went from 80/20 to 0/100 in a few months. Mitchell Hashimoto says entire companies are now in AI psychosis and can’t be reasoned with about it. Garry Tan told a SXSW crowd he’s sleeping four hours a night because he can’t put Claude Code down, and that a third of the CEOs he knows are the same. He called it “cyber psychosis.” (His assistant later told TechCrunch he was joking.)
